bsm_11.message: thumbs through a clipboard that has clearly been rained on.

bsm_12.text: Most nights it's not violence. Most nights it's somebody cold, or somebody owed.

bsm_13.text: People think the stars mean you're dangerous. Stars just mean somebody saw you.

bsm_14.message: glances at the camera, then away, like he regrets agreeing to this.

bsm_15.text: I've apologised to more people than I've arrested. Put that in the show. They won't.

bsm_18.text: A young runner is up against a wall, hands flat, breathing hard. A vacuum-sealed brick of something green sits on the pavement between him and the officer.

bsm_2.text: ♪ A cheap, swaggering guitar riff kicks in — four chords, no budget, enormous confidence. ♪

bsm_21.message: crouches, tags the brick, and writes on the tag with a pen that doesn't work until the fourth try.

bsm_22.text: Under Basin ordinance, possession at this weight is three stars and a night in Precinct 9.

bsm_23.text: The suspect's chief concern is not the night in Precinct 9.

bsm_24.text: Hey. Look at me. When did you last back up?

bsm_25.message: waits. The answer takes a while.

bsm_26.text: Yeah. Well. Try not to die before Thursday, then.

bsm_28.text: The South Gate. A queue of people stands in the cold with their arms out while a scanner arch clicks over them, one at a time, forever.

bsm_32.text: Everybody coming into this city gets searched. Everybody. I've searched the man who signs my cheques.

bsm_35.text: I found a knife once. In a boot. It was a really good find.

bsm_36.message: looks at Kessler for confirmation. He does not get it.

bsm_38.text: That was nine months ago, Quill.

bsm_40.text: It was a really good find.

bsm_41.text: Trooper Quill has been at the South Gate for two years and has recovered one knife.

bsm_42.text: He has recovered it repeatedly, in conversation, ever since.

bsm_47.text: Belt. Laces. Anything sharp, anything that talks to anything else.

bsm_48.message: drops a handful of personal effects into a tray with the enthusiasm of a man filing his own paperwork.

bsm_49.text: Legal property comes back when you walk. Contraband goes in the locker downstairs.

bsm_5.text: The Basin at night, shot from a low drone: wet asphalt, sodium light, steam coming up through the grates. Somewhere below, a siren starts and then thinks better of it.

bsm_50.text: Nothing comes out of the locker downstairs.

bsm_51.text: A folded orange jumpsuit is pushed across the counter. It has been washed so many times it has gone the colour of weak tea.

bsm_52.text: Three stars. Three minutes a star. In Coldwater, the sentence is served in real time, and the clock does not care that you are bored.

bsm_53.text: Some of them cry. Some of them sleep. The ones who've been through a vat, they just sit there and stare at the wall like they're waiting for it to buffer.

bsm_55.text: Vale's cruiser, parked. Engine ticking as it cools. He does not get out for a long moment.

bsm_57.text: People ask if it gets to you.

bsm_58.text: It's a job. You do the job. Then you go home and you sit in your kitchen with the light off for a bit, and then you're fine.

bsm_59.message: gets out, closes the door quietly, and walks up to apartment six without looking back at the camera.

bsm_60.text: Sergeant Vale will be back on shift in nine hours.

bsm_61.text: Coldwater's Finest. Filmed on location, with the cooperation of people who had no realistic way to decline.
